title: Tummy Tuck or Mommy Makeover: Which One Do You Need?
meta_description: A tummy tuck treats the abdomen; a mommy makeover adds the breasts and can add liposuction. Compare who each one suits, how recovery differs and the risks.
excerpt: A tummy tuck treats the abdomen. A mommy makeover adds the breasts and can add liposuction. Compare what each one treats, who each one suits and how recovery and risk change when surgeries are combined, then use the decision table to see which one fits.
quick_answer:
Should I get a tummy tuck or a mommy makeover?

A tummy tuck treats the abdomen alone. A mommy makeover adds a breast procedure and can add liposuction, so more of your body heals at once. In one large database, major complications followed 3.1% of tummy tucks alone and 4.6% of those with liposuction and a breast procedure (Winocour and colleagues, 2015).

quotes: Usually, around the three-month mark, you can return to your normal activities, although it can take six months to a year before you see your final mommy makeover results.

sources.title: Mommy Makeover
quotes: The combination of procedures typically focuses on your breasts and abdomen and might include a tummy tuck, a breast procedure such as a lift, augmentation or reduction, and liposuction of the leg, arms, hips, or waist.
Pregnancy or weight gain following these surgeries may compromise your results.
You will likely have scars following these procedures hidden in your bikini line or under your bra.
If you get breast implants, you will need to replace them over time.
The recovery time is at least two weeks but could be longer depending on your specific combination of procedures.

sources.title: Mommy makeover: aftercare and recovery
quotes: The tummy tuck component of a “mommy makeover” is the most uncomfortable.
Plan to take about two weeks off from work, depending on the physical demands of your job.
You may be comfortable enough to drive a car in two or three weeks or when all of your sutures and drains are removed, and you are no longer taking pain medication.
You won't feel like yourself for at least seven to ten days, and you still shouldn't do any heavy lifting (such as picking up your children or baskets of laundry) for four to six weeks.
If you have small children, you must put someone else totally in charge of their care for at least two weeks.

sources.title: Mommy Makeovers: How They Work and What To Expect
quotes: You’ll need to quit smoking for at least six weeks prior to surgery.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck (Abdominoplasty)
quotes: It could take up to up to three months to see the final result.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck Scar
quotes: The scar for a standard tummy tuck usually spans your abdomen, from hip bone to hip bone, just above your pubic area.
You may also have a scar around your belly button.
Avoid heavy lifting, strenuous exercise, sexual activity and stretching until your provider says it’s safe to do these activities (usually four to eight weeks after the procedure).

sources.title: Risks and Complications of Breast Implants
quotes: Breast implants are not considered lifetime devices.
Some complications will require more surgery.

sources.title: Abdominoplasty: Risk Factors, Complication Rates, and Safety of Combined Procedures (Winocour and colleagues, 2015)
quotes: The authors identified 25,478 abdominoplasties from 183,914 procedures in the database.
Of these, 31.5 percent were hematomas, 27.2 percent were infections and 20.2 percent were suspected or confirmed venous thromboembolism.

On multivariate analysis, significant risk factors (p < 0.05) included male sex (relative risk, 1.8), age 55 years or older (1.4), body mass index greater than or equal to 30 (1.3), multiple procedures (1.5), and procedure performance in a hospital or surgical center versus office-based surgical suite (1.6).

Combined procedures increased the risk of complication (abdominoplasty alone, 3.1 percent; with liposuction, 3.8 percent; breast procedure, 4.3 percent; liposuction and breast procedure, 4.6 percent; body-contouring procedure, 6.8 percent; liposuction and body-contouring procedure, 10.4 percent).

sources.title: Venous Thromboembolism in the Cosmetic Patient: Analysis of 129,007 Patients (Winocour and colleagues, 2017)
quotes: Primary outcome was occurrence of a clinically significant VTE within 30 days of surgery.
Combined procedures had a significantly higher overall rate of VTE compared to solitary procedures (0.20% vs 0.04%, P < .01).
The incidence of VTE after cosmetic procedures is relatively low.

sources.title: Risk of Concomitant Abdominoplasty and Breast Surgery versus Isolated Procedures: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis (Skorochod and Wolf, 2026)
quotes: Eight studies encompassing 138,020 patients were included.
Certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low.
Concomitant abdominoplasty and breast surgery carries a complication profile comparable to abdominoplasty alone but elevated relative to breast surgery alone.
These findings suggest that combined procedures are generally safe in carefully selected patients.

sources.title: The impact of operative time on complications after plastic surgery: a multivariate regression analysis of 1753 cases (Hardy and colleagues, 2014)
quotes: Each hour increase in surgery duration was associated with a 21% rise in odds of morbidity (P < .0001).

sources.title: The Safety and Effects of Pregnancy after Abdominoplasty: A Systematic Review of the Literature (Karunaratne and colleagues, 2023)
quotes: 17 studies encompassing 237 patients met inclusion.
There were no neonatal or maternal mortalities in any study.
Pregnancy should not be contraindicated after abdominoplasty.

sources.title: Rule 64B8-9.009, Standard of Care for Office Surgery
quotes: When combined with abdominoplasty, liposuction may not exceed 1000cc of supernatant fat
the maximum planned duration of all surgical procedures combined must not exceed 8 hours
